title: XZ compressed file format
summary: XZ is a container format for LZMA2-compressed data. Structure: 6-byte header magic (0xFD '7zXZ' 0x00), 2-byte flags, then blocks (each with a block header, compressed data, and integrity check), an index, and a 12-byte footer (2-byte flags, 4-byte backward size, 6-byte footer magic 0x59 0x5A).

structure.meaning: 1 byte (reserved, must be 0) + 1 byte (check type: 0 none, 1 CRC32, 4 CRC64, 10 SHA-256).
Block header (size, flags, filters, compressed size, uncompressed size) + LZMA2 compressed data + integrity check.
Number of records + (unpadded size, unpadded size of block) pairs + CRC32 of the index.

Flags (2) + backward size (4, /4) + footer magic 0x59 0x5A (2, 'YZ') + ... actually 2-byte flags + 4-byte backward size + 2-byte magic YZ + 2 reserved = 12? Let me be precise: 2 (flags) + 4 (backward size) + 2 (magic YZ) = 8, plus 4 reserved = 12.

ext.example_decoded: XZ header magic + flags (no check type, CRC64 default)
notes: XZ uses LZMA2, which allows uncompressed chunks and dictionary reset between blocks.
Integrity checks: none, CRC32, CRC64 (default), or SHA-256.
XZ is used by Linux kernel (module compression), tar (tar.xz), and many package managers.
The index enables random access to individual blocks.
